name: Glass Dusk
texts: A small line under each number: installed, in how many games, average completion, drives.
Achievement progress of the game on the Continue card.
Behind the Shift+Tab panels: a light veil or Steam's dark sheet.
Colour of buttons and highlights. Fixed uses Accent from the Colors tab.
Cover: the focused game's art fills the screen and lends its colour.
Every game in the library, installed or not.
Game Overview, browser and toolbar: smoked glass or Steam's own.
Hours played in the last two weeks.
How strongly the game art shows through.
Millennium plugins that draw their own interface (HLTB for Steam, Achievement Groups, Player Count, Extendium): in the theme's colours, or as the plugin ships them.
Point at a cover in the recently played row: a card with the game's screenshots, its name and hours. The store's screenshots are fetched from Steam at that moment.
Smoked glass over the art of the game you have open: the client takes its accent colour from that art. Styles the library, store, menus, Big Picture and the in-game overlay.
Space taken in Steam's library folders, in GB.
Steam's What's New shelf on the library home.
Steam's row for adding a shelf to the library home.
Text the theme draws itself: home header, Big Picture chip, dates.

The account chooser when Steam starts (Who's playing?): the art of the game you played last, plain dusk or Steam's wall of covers, each with the theme's glass, or Steam's own look. It shows only if Steam asks which account to use.
The collections a game is in, shown at the top right of its art on the game page, as Steam does. A click opens the collection.
The row of recently played games under the Continue card.
The theme's header (greeting, stats, Continue) or Steam's shelves only.
Top-left chip: logo, hours played, last played.
Where the Continue card and the recently played row take their games: only what is installed on this machine, or everything in the library.

Your game list beside the store and other web pages of the main window: off, pinned there, coming out when you point at the window's edge, or a rail of your last games' covers that opens into the list.
